                                          PUC PROJECT No. 58481

                                                      §
Rulemaking to Implement                               §         Public Utility Commission
Large Load Interconnection                            §
Standards Under PURA § 37.0561                        §                  of Texas


    EdgeConneX’s Comments on PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication filed on February 13, 2026

                                                I.        Introduction
         EdgeConneX1 (“ECX”) greatly appreciates the hard work that Staff at the Public Utility
Commission of Texas (“PUCT” or “Commission”) has done in developing a proposed rule to
implement Section 37.0561 of the Public Utility Regulatory Act (“PURA”). ECX recognizes that
this is an important and complex task, especially since the interconnection standards that are
developed in this project will directly impact what loads are included in Batch Zero and the
ongoing batch study process that is currently being developed by ERCOT.                                Because the
Commission will be considering and potentially approving PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication
that was filed on February 13, 2026,2 at this Thursday’s March 12th open meeting, and the
Commission-approved proposed rule’s standards will be added to ERCOT’s Planning Guide
Revision Request (“PGRR”) 145 that implements Batch Zero, ECX respectfully files these
comments ahead of the March 12th open meeting to raise specific concerns with PUCT Staff’s
Proposal for Publication for the Commission’s consideration.


                II.       Specific Concerns with PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication
         As stated in prior comments filed in this project, ECX supports the development of large
load interconnection standards that are proportionate with actual risk, fair in application to all
Large Load (LL) customers, and aligned with furthering economic development in the state. ECX,
therefore, highlights the following five specific concerns with PUCT Staff’s proposed rule:




1

global leader in anytime, anywhere, and any scale data center services for a diverse portfolio of industries, including
Cloud, AI, Content, Networks, and a robust suite of customers.
2
 See PUCT Staff’s Memo and Proposal for Publication for consideration at the February 20, 2026, Open Meeting,
Project No. 58481 (February 13, 2026).


                                                          1
 1. Front loading of costly requirements in the Intermediate Agreement stage in proposed
   Section (d) when a LL customer has no clear line of site for interconnection and
   energization. Subsection (d)(1) of the proposed rule includes stringent site control
   requirements that require a LL customer to take costly action through either a lease or
   purchase of land for a proposed site location at an early stage in the development process
   when an interconnection study hasn’t even been started or completed by an interconnecting
   distribution service provider (“DSP”) or interconnecting transmission service provider
   (“TSP”) and ERCOT. At this early stage, more flexibility should be provided to a LL
   customer to at least allow Purchase and Sale Agreements, Options to Purchase, Right of
   First Refusal, Right of First Offer, and/or Exclusivity Agreements to establish site control
   of a proposed site location. Furthermore, the financial security on a dollar per MW basis
   for requested peak demand in Subsection (d)(10) and financial security for long lead time
   equipment or services in Subsection (d)(11) are also very costly upfront requirements at an
   early stage where there is no clear line of site for interconnection or energization and an
   interconnection study has not begun or has been completed by an interconnecting DSP or
   TSP. The financial security at this Intermediate Agreement stage should focus on actual
   study, engineering, and procurement costs that are made on behalf of a LL customer. The
   financial security posted at this Intermediate Agreement stage, after all outstanding
   balances are paid off by an interconnecting DSP or TSP, should be fully refunded to the LL
   customer if the LL customer decides to withdraw its LLI request for the proposed site
   location.

2. The non-refundable interconnection fee of $100,000 per MW of contracted peak
   demand at the Interconnection Agreement stage in proposed Subsection (f)(7) is
   unnecessary given the fact that a LL customer will already have to pay 100% of its
   direct interconnection costs through contribution in aid of construction (“CIAC”)
   and post financial security for long lead time equipment or services and transmission
   system upgrades. This additional cost has no direct tie to actual system costs and cost
   causation principles and only serves to add an additional unnecessary cost burden for LL
   customers. Moreover, allowing the interconnection fee to be used as an offset to an
   interconnecting TSP’s rate base could result in over-collection of revenue and unnecessary
   ratemaking complications that could be better addressed with other approaches, like a
   minimum demand charge in an interconnecting TSP’s tariff.

3. The financial security requirements at the Intermediate Agreement stage and
   Interconnection Agreement stage have a compounding, pancaking effect. At the
   Intermediate Agreement stage, a LL customer must post financial security of $100,000 per
   MW of requested peak demand and financial security for long-lead time equipment or
   services under proposed Subsection (d)(10) and (11). At the Interconnection Agreement
   stage, a LL customer must pay a non-refundable interconnection fee of $100,000 per MW
   of contracted peak demand and post financial security for long-lead time equipment or
   services under proposed Subsection (f)(7) and (8). A literal reading of the proposed rule
   could be interpreted to require a cumulative $200,000 per MW total of financial security at
   both the Intermediate Agreement and Interconnection Agreement stage. The proposed rule
   should be clarified if this is not the intent of the rule so that LL customers know exactly
   how much financial security will be required at each stage and what financial security


                                            2
        carries over from the Intermediate Agreement stage to the Interconnection Agreement
       stage.

   4. The 80/20% refund split between the interconnecting TSP and a LL customer in
      proposed Subsection (g)(3) and (4) that applies when a LL customer withdraws all or
      a portion of its requested or contracted peak demand and proposed subsection (h)(3)
      and (4) that applies when a LL customer fails to meet a milestone in its energization
      schedule is inequitable, is misaligned with cost causation principles, and serves as an
      unnecessary penalty on LL customers. If an interconnecting TSP has already applied the
      LL customer’s financial security to all outstanding amounts owed, a LL customer should
      get the entire 100% of the remaining balance back since all costs incurred by the
      interconnecting TSP on the LL customer’s behalf have been recovered. There are no more
      interconnection-related costs that need to be paid for by a LL customer at this point.
      Allowing the interconnecting TSP to keep 80% of the remaining balance to apply as an
      offset to its rate base is an unfair and unnecessary penalty for LL customers.


   5. A LL customer that pays, in full, for long lead time equipment should be allowed to
      take the equipment to another proposed site location. The proposed rule should allow
      a LL customer, rather than the interconnecting DSP or TSP, to keep long lead time
      equipment that has been paid for in its entirety by the LL customer for use at another site
      location. The proposed rule should be amended to allow the LL customer to have this right.

                                        III.   Conclusion
       ECX appreciates PUCT Staff’s hard work on this proposed rule and the Commission’s
consideration of the concerns raised in these comments.


                                    Respectfully submitted
                                    Diane Hopingardner
                                    Senior Manager – Energy Development
                                    EdgeConneX
                                    2201 Cooperative Way, Suite 400
                                    Herndon, VA 20171
                                    dhopingardner@edgeconnex.com
